_: Kill-check for asc-09wx.8.3's second half: `asc handlers grade <entry-id>`, the command that reads an intervention row's OWN metric rather than a handler path someone typed, proves the ruler has not moved since the row was written, and prints that row's comparison and power figure (packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/grade.ts). Eight mutants, one per claim. The two that matter most are the pair of verifications the command exists for: `ruler-hash-not-checked` lets a handler whose `where` clause was edited be graded against a baseline taken under the old one, and `derive-version-not-checked` compares units counted from two different derivations of the same log. Both are invisible in every other way -- the numbers still print, and they are the right shape. `split-at-now-not-the-rows-own-date` is the third of that family: it makes the comparison a window chosen at read time instead of the one the row pre-registered, which is the difference between a test and a number somebody went looking for. The rest are the refusals and the last sentence. Killers were found empirically, by planting each mutant and reading the failing test names off vitest's JSON reporter, not by guessing them. NOTE the harness runs with --allow-dirty: this spec's target is uncommitted while asc-09wx.8.3 is open, and the restore's sha256 check is what makes that safe.
